# Alignment test fixtures

Plain-text German / English book pairs used by the alignment tests (plan.md §1.1, step 6).
They are generated by `npm run fixtures` (`tools/fetch-fixtures.ts`) from Project Gutenberg and
committed, so tests and CI never hit the network. Re-run the script only to change the manifest
in `tools/gutenberg.ts` or to pick up a corrected Gutenberg edition.

| File | Work | Gutenberg # | Starts at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kafka-verwandlung.de.txt` | Kafka, *Die Verwandlung* (Kurt Wolff, 1917) | 22367 | `I.` |
| `kafka-verwandlung.en.txt` | Kafka, *Metamorphosis*, tr. David Wyllie | 5200 | `I` |
| `goethe-werther.de.txt` | Goethe, *Die Leiden des jungen Werther* (Hamburger Ausgabe) | 2407 + 2408 | `Erstes Buch` / `Zweites Buch` |
| `goethe-werther.en.txt` | Goethe, *The Sorrows of Young Werther*, tr. R. D. Boylan | 2527 | `PREFACE` |

## What the script strips

- Everything outside the `*** START OF …` / `*** END OF …` markers (Gutenberg header and
  licence text).
- Transcriber credits after the START marker and "Ende dieses Projekt Gutenberg Etextes …"
  notes before the END marker.
- The title page, publisher and edition lines before the first heading named above.
- A BOM, CRLF line endings and trailing whitespace on each line.

Nothing inside the work is rewritten: Gutenberg's 72-column hard wrapping, double spaces after
sentences in the German Werther, and blank-line runs before headings are left as they are. The
`txt` importer is expected to cope with all of that.

## Things to know when aligning these

- **Werther DE** is two Gutenberg volumes joined into one file; the second starts at
  `Zweites Buch`. Letters are headed `Am 4. Mai 1771` / `Den 17. Mai`; the editor's narration
  starts at `Der Herausgeber an den Leser`.
- **Werther EN** keeps Boylan's short `PREFACE`, which this German edition does not include, so
  the first English section has no German counterpart. Books are `BOOK I` / `BOOK II.`, letters
  are `MAY 4.` style, and the narration starts at `THE EDITOR TO THE READER.`
- **Kafka** has three parts on each side (`I.` / `II.` / `III.` in German, `I` / `II` / `III` in
  English).

## Licences

The German texts by Kafka and Goethe are in the public domain. R. D. Boylan's 19th-century
translation is in the public domain. David Wyllie's translation of *Metamorphosis* is
copyrighted by the translator and is distributed by Project Gutenberg under the
[Project Gutenberg License](https://www.gutenberg.org/policy/license.html), which permits
copying and redistribution; it is included here unmodified apart from the stripping described
above, for testing only, with this attribution in place of the removed header.
